# dsh-plugin-guard
**A security gate you can run before you install a DSH plugin, before you publish one, and in CI.**
[](https://github.com/RyeSama/dsh-plugin-guard/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [](https://www.npmjs.com/pa
ckage/dsh-plugin-guard-cli) [](LICENSE)
DSH plugins are npm packages that declare a `dsh` block and get composed into the DSH host process.
There is no sandbox at that boundary: a plugin runs with the same privileges as DSH itself. This too
l does not change that. It makes the decision *visible before it happens*:

- **scanner** — reads the package (never runs it) and reports what it would be allowed to do
- **per
mission manifest** — `dsh.permissions`, a convention this project proposes so a plugin can state wha

t it reads, writes, executes and sends
- **trust index** — a local record of the source hash you rev

iewed, so a silent republish is visible
- **runtime audit adapter** — a documented interface with a
sidecar implementation, honest about what DSH does not expose today
It is deliberately not a sandbox, not an antivirus, and not a replacement for reading the code.
## What a scan looks at
| Area | Examples of what is flagged |
| DSH manifest | no `dsh` block, `bundle.patch` pointing at a file that is not shipped, unparsable D

SH version range |
| npm state | not published, deprecated, local version ahead of the published one

|
| Permissions | no `dsh.permissions`, invalid declaration, code using a capability it never decla

red |
| Dangerous code | `child_process`, `eval`/`new Function`, `vm.runIn*`, dynamic `require`/`imp

ort`, `process.binding`, obfuscated blobs |
| Install scripts | `preinstall`, `install`, `postinstal

l` — code that runs on `npm install`, before any review |
| Dependencies | missing lockfile, `*` / `

latest` / git / http specs, very large dependency surface |
| Network | hard-coded hosts that the pl

ugin never declared |
| Source integrity | package hash differs from the one recorded in your trust
index, publisher changed |
`dsh-plugin-guard rules` prints the full list with severities.
## Commands

h `dsh-plugin-guard` and `dsh-guard` are installed as binaries, so `npx dsh-guard scan .` works too.
### Exit codes
| Code | Meaning |

| `0` | pass, or warnings only |
| `1` | at least one high finding (or any medium finding with `--fa

il-on-medium`) |
| `2` | bad usage — unknown option, unknown rule id, bad `--max-files` |
| `3` | th
e scan could not run — target not found, network failure, unreadable package |
CI usage:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Zero config
There is no config file and no `init` step required. Defaults: all rules on, network off for directo
ry scans, readable report on, exit code on high risk. Flags are the only knobs:
`--json`, `--offline`, `--check-publish`, `--only <ids>`, `--ignore <ids>`, `--fail-on-medium`, `--d
sh-version <v>`, `--max-files <n>`, `--record`, `--verbose`.
## Declaring permissions
`dsh.permissions` is a **convention proposed by this project**. DSH itself does not read it today, a
nd the scanner cannot enforce it at runtime — it only checks that the declaration exists, is valid,
and matches what the code actually does.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The full field reference, semantics and examples are in docs/permissions-spec.md.
## Trust index
The index is a small JSON file at `~/.dsh-plugin-guard/index.json` (override with `DSH_GUARD_INDEX`)
. It stores, per `name@version`, the package hash, tree hash, publisher, scan verdict and the DSH ve
rsion used. Scanning works with or without it — when an entry is missing for a registry package the
report says the source is unverified instead of pretending it is safe.
`index add` records what you reviewed. If a later scan of the same `name@version` sees a different t
ree hash or publisher, that is reported as a high finding: the artefact changed after review.
## Runtime audit: what is real and what is not
DSH has no public plugin audit stream and no in-process isolation. This project therefore ships:

- a documented `RuntimeAuditAdapter` interface (src/audit/types.ts),
- a **sidecar** implementation

that appends NDJSON events to `~/.dsh-plugin-guard/audit.ndjson`,
- `audit status` which prints, in
plain words, that no official hook exists (src/adapters/dsh/index.ts).
It never claims to intercept, block or observe plugin code it cannot see. See docs/audit-adapter.md
and docs/threat-model.md.
## Inside DSH
The same scanner ships as a DSH plugin bundle, so the agent can check a package before it installs o
same scanner ships as a DSH plugin bundle, so the agent can check a package before it installs one:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It registers one tool, `plugin_guard`. You pass a directory or an npm package name; it answers with
the verdict, the reasons and the next command — the same output as the CLI, without a terminal.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The bundle has no client code, so nothing is added to the desktop UI. It is a
separate npm package (

plugins/dsh-guard-tool) because
DSH resolves a bundle through its own manifest: a package either is

a bundle or
is a CLI, and pretending to be both would make the admission path unclear.
## Security statement
The scanner only reads files. It does not `require`/`import` the scanned package, does not execute `
postinstall`, does not resolve its dependencies, and does not write anything into the scanned folder
. Network access happens only for `scan <npm-package>`, `--check-publish`, `index add <npm-package>`
and `doctor`. Reports contain no secrets: file paths are relative to the package root.
If you find a way to make the scanner execute scanned code, that is a security bug — please open an
find a way to make the scanner execute scanned code, that is a security bug — please open an issue.
